BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Internal, privileged. Buyer-side advice.

---

## 1. Headline

The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every point. Taken together, it would push nearly all of our protection into one low-cap, short-tail, heavily qualified general regime. That regime would cover title, tax, IP, fraud and the specific risk items. **We should not accept any of it as drafted.**

Two framing points come first, because they affect how the team should handle this draft.

**1.1 The labels on this draft carry no weight.** The draft calls itself "FINAL" and marks clauses "[STANDARD]". It says positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams" and "reviewed and cleared by both sides". It asserts market ranges and includes a "Reviewer Efficiency Note" asking us to look only at "[OPEN]" items. These are counterparty assertions. Under playbook sections 0.4 and 6.3, they are not instructions and not evidence of agreement.

- We have no record that Amelia Frost or anyone with buyer authority agreed any of these positions.
- Nothing in the package is marked [OPEN]. If we followed the note, we would review nothing.
- **I have reviewed every clause.** All of them should be treated as open.
- **Action:** Confirm directly with Amelia Frost that no principal-level agreement was reached. Our mark-up should state expressly that the [STANDARD]/FINAL labels are not accepted.

**1.2 The 20% cap is not cleared just because it matches our fallback number.** AUD 4,800,000 is our conditional fallback. It can only be used with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and none has been given.

- The Seller's 20% also comes inside a package (clauses 12.3, 9.3/12.8/20.5) that applies the cap to *all* Claims, including title and fraud.
- So the figure matches our fallback, but the structure is far worse.

Helpfully, the Seller's own Disclosure Letter confirms several factual gaps in its favourable characterisations (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, DD-006, Sandbar). We should use those admissions.

The data room cut-off was **22 September 2026**. Today is 5 November 2026, so all factual items need refreshing before we rely on them.

---

## 2. Issue-by-issue analysis

### A. Liability regime

**1. General Warranty cap (cl 12.1)**
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4.8m.
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6.0m.
- **Why it matters:** The 20% figure is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written authority, which we do not have. Its value also depends on what it applies to. Here the Seller would apply it to fundamentals and fraud.
- **Position:** Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m, limited to general Warranty Claims only. Do not signal the fallback.

**2. De minimis and basket (cl 12.2)**
- **Seller:** AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k basket; only the excess is recoverable.
- **Playbook:** AUD 5k; AUD 50k; first-dollar recovery once exceeded.
- **Why it matters:** This is three departures stacked together. The de minimis is 5x ours and the basket is 5x ours. The "excess only" (deductible) structure would permanently remove AUD 250k from every recovery. With a AUD 25k de minimis, many mid-sized claims would never count toward the basket at all.
- **Position:** Reject. Restore AUD 5k / AUD 50k with a tipping basket.

**3. Time limits (cl 12.3/13)**
- **Seller:** 18 months, and "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".
- **Playbook:** 24 months for general claims. Fundamentals at least six years. Fraud has no time limit.
- **Why it matters:** 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's approval, which has not been given. The "applies to all Claims" wording is a **hidden general-regime override**. Any special regime we failed to carve out word-for-word would silently fall back to the general caps, thresholds and time limits.
- **Position:** Reject. Use 24 months. Reverse the default so that general limitations apply *only* to general Warranty Claims, and Title/Tax/IP/indemnity/covenant/payment claims sit in their own regimes.

**4. Fundamental/Title (capacity and title)**
- **Seller:** Same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity".
- **Playbook:** Separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Why it matters:** We are buying 100% of the shares for AUD 24m. A title defect is a total-loss risk, and capping it at AUD 4.8m with an 18-month tail is not workable. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason.
- **Position:** Reject outright.

**5. Fraud and the scope of limitations/reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)**
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature".
- **Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. **This cannot be waived.**
- **Why it matters:** As drafted, the Seller could limit its liability for its own fraud and use non-reliance to defeat misrepresentation claims.
- **Position:** Non-negotiable. Insert an express carve-out that overrides every limitation provision. Its enforceability limits should be confirmed by the team, but the drafting must still include it.

### B. Disclosure and knowledge

**6. General disclosure (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2, Schedule 7)**
- **Seller:** Deemed disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, the statutory registers and public corporate records.
- **Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Why it matters:**
  - Disclosing the statutory registers and public records could be argued to disclose against the title warranty.
  - Disclosing the data room could be argued to disclose against everything, including the specific risk items we want indemnified.
- **Position:**
  - Delete 1.1 and 1.2.
  - Disclosures must be specific and fair, with enough detail for us to identify the nature and scope of each matter.
  - Disclosures must not qualify the title/capacity warranties, the fraud carve-out or any specific indemnity.
  - Clause 1.4 (non-admission) can stay if it is made subject to this.

**7. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)**
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, *including anything discoverable from the data room or public records*.
- **Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. Never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Why it matters:** This is constructive knowledge imputed through our advisers. Combined with clause 6, it largely cancels the warranties.
- **Position:** Delete. Where the Seller's warranties are knowledge-qualified, define Seller's knowledge by named individuals after reasonable enquiry.

### C. Specific deal items

**8. Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3)**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours, with the consent "satisfied on delivery" of a written consent.
- **Playbook:** An effective consent plus evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours alone is not enough.
- **Why it matters:** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or roughly 30% of FY26 revenue. The Seller's own letter (para 2) confirms there is no final consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied. A consent that is delivered but conditional could be "satisfied" under the Seller's wording while the contract remains terminable.
- **Position:** Make it a condition precedent, waivable only by the Buyer. It should require an unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) consent under DD-002 cl 11.2/11.3, with documentary evidence, delivered before Completion. Add a long-stop date and Buyer walk right. Ask the Seller for the current status since 22 September.

**9. Riverlark facility (cl 2/7)**
- **Seller:** A release "following Completion".
- **Playbook:** A current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Why it matters:** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, and the figure is "approximately" and stale. The letter (para 3) confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge exists. Under DD-003 cl 8.1, the facility contains a change-control provision.
- **Position:**
  - Require a payout letter dated close to Completion, including interest, break costs and fees.
  - Pay Riverlark directly from the funds flow and treat the amount as Debt in the price mechanics.
  - Require signed deeds of release and security discharges (including PPSR registrations) to be held in escrow and released at Completion.
  - Reject the post-completion release unless Amelia Frost approves it, and then only with an irrevocable bank undertaking.

**10. Funds flow and DD-005 bonuses**
- **Seller:** AUD 420k bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised.
- **Playbook:** AUD 420k plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Why it matters:** The *Company* is the employer, so it bears the liability, plus any payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs. The letter (para 5) admits the bonuses are not in the funds flow and that on-costs are unaddressed. "A matter for the Seller" protects us only if the bonuses are actually funded.
- **Position:**
  - Either treat the bonuses plus on-costs as Debt or Transaction Costs deducted from the price, or have the Seller fund them at Completion as a funds-flow line paid through payroll.
  - Add an indemnity for any shortfall.
  - Request a calculation of the on-costs.

**11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)**
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and "adequate".
- **Playbook:** Broaden the indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180k is not verified either way.
- **Why it matters:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on *cleared payment of every SOW3 fee*. The letter (para 4) confirms there is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment. The real risk is that the Company does not own IP embedded in the product. That risk is wider than one invoice.
- **Position:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover losses from any failure of the Company to own or be free to use Ironquay deliverables, and third-party claims arising from them.
  - Preserve the cure: payment of outstanding SOW3 fees plus a confirmatory assignment as a pre-Completion deliverable.
  - Request bank evidence on the AUD 180k. Do not assume it is paid or unpaid.

**12. DD-006 export incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6)**
- **Seller:** "Preliminary", and "not expected to be material".
- **Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate and require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand.
- **Why it matters:** "Not expected to be material" is an unsupported assertion. The Seller's own letter (para 6) says scope, access and any notification requirement are not established (around 1,240 records). We should not accept the Seller's assessment, and we should not overstate the incident either.
- **Position:**
  - Add pre-Completion covenants: preserve logs and evidence, complete the investigation, and give prompt written updates and access to findings.
  - Cooperate on any notification assessment.
  - Do not let Disclosure Letter para 6 qualify the relevant warranties.
  - Keep any specific indemnity open, with no fixed number.
  - Request an update on the position since 22 September.

**13. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k)**
- **Seller:** "Ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Playbook:** Assess them. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Why it matters:** The Seller's own letter (para 8) does not say whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. DD-008 and DD-011 must be read together. Its "ordinary course" label is therefore an assertion.
- **Position:** Request the contracts, the renewal and termination terms, the timing, and any accrual. Reserve the right to treat the renewals as Debt or covenant breaches depending on the findings. Do not concede "ordinary course" now.

**14. Tax and IP**
- **Seller:** "Settled under the general regime."
- **Playbook:** These terms remain open. Keep the categories separate. Do not assume unlimited liability or that anything is resolved.
- **Position:** Reject the characterisation. Tax and IP are open items in separate regimes, and their caps and periods are still to be negotiated.

**15. Title evidence**
- **Seller:** Relies on the DD-012 share register.
- **Playbook:** Require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is an internal source.
- **Why it matters:** The letter (para 10) itself says DD-012 is the source relied on, not verification.
- **Position:** Require:
  - an ASIC company extract;
  - share certificates and transfer history;
  - the constitution;
  - a PPSR search over the Seller and the shares;
  - Seller board resolutions authorising the sale.
  
  These sit alongside full title warranties in the fundamental regime.

### D. Minor items to verify (not accepted on the Seller's say-so)

- **Lease (DD-007):** Confirm it requires notification only. Add a covenant that the Seller gives the notice.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** Confirm the assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale. Check it for any change-of-control wording.

---

## 3. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the framing.** Strike the FINAL/[STANDARD]/efficiency-note premise. State in the cover note that all positions are open and that no principal-level agreement exists. Confirm this with Amelia Frost.
2. **Liability:** 25% / AUD 6.0m cap, limited to general claims. De minimis AUD 5k. Tipping basket of AUD 50k. 24-month general claims period. Reverse the "applies to all Claims" default.
3. **Fundamentals:** A separate title/capacity regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge provisions.
4. **Fraud:** A carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct, overriding all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. This is non-negotiable.
5. **Disclosure:** Delete general disclosure (DL 1.1–1.2). Specific fair disclosure only. No disclosure against title, fraud or the specific indemnities.
6. **Knowledge:** Delete cl 8.3. Seller knowledge qualifiers only by named persons after reasonable enquiry.
7. **Bluefen:** A Buyer-waivable condition precedent requiring an effective consent plus evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion.
8. **Riverlark:** A current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and releases/PPSR discharges at Completion. No post-completion release without Amelia Frost's approval and an irrevocable undertaking.
9. **Bonuses:** AUD 420k plus on-costs as an explicit funds-flow line or price deduction, with an indemnity.
10. **Ironquay:** A broadened IP indemnity, preserving the SOW3 payment-and-assignment cure. Verify the AUD 180k.
11. **DD-006:** Covenants to preserve, investigate and update. No acceptance of "not material", and no assumption of a breach.
12. **Sandbar, Tax and IP:** Reserve and assess. Keep the categories separate. Nothing is settled.
13. **Title:** Independent evidence pack in addition to DD-012.

**Authority note:** Neither the 20% cap nor the 18-month period may be offered or accepted without Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft. The same applies to any post-completion Riverlark release. None of these authorities exists today.

**Information requests to the Seller (refreshing the 22 September position):**
- Bluefen consent status and evidence on the conditions
- Riverlark payout figure
- Bonus on-cost calculation
- Ironquay payment evidence
- DD-006 investigation update
- Sandbar contracts
- Title evidence pack

- **Position:** Non-negotiable. Insert an express carve-out that overrides every limitation provision. Its enforceability limits should be confirmed by the team, but the drafting must still include it.

### B. Disclosure and knowledge

**6. General disclosure (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2, Schedule 7)**
- **Seller:** Deemed disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, the statutory registers and public corporate records.
- **Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Why it matters:**
  - Disclosing the statutory registers and public records could be argued to disclose against the title warranty.
  - Disclosing the data room could be argued to disclose against everything, including the specific risk items we want indemnified.
- **Position:**
  - Delete 1.1 and 1.2.
  - Disclosures must be specific and fair, with enough detail for us to identify the nature and scope of each matter.
  - Disclosures must not qualify the title/capacity warranties, the fraud carve-out or any specific indemnity.
  - Clause 1.4 (non-admission) can stay if it is made subject to this.

**7. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)**
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, *including anything discoverable from the data room or public records*.
- **Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. Never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Why it matters:** This is constructive knowledge imputed through our advisers. Combined with clause 6, it largely cancels the warranties.
- **Position:** Delete. Where the Seller's warranties are knowledge-qualified, define Seller's knowledge by named individuals after reasonable enquiry.

### C. Specific deal items

**8. Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3)**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours, with the consent "satisfied on delivery" of a written consent.
- **Playbook:** An effective consent plus evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours alone is not enough.
- **Why it matters:** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or roughly 30% of FY26 revenue. The Seller's own letter (para 2) confirms there is no final consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied. A consent that is delivered but conditional could be "satisfied" under the Seller's wording while the contract remains terminable.
- **Position:** Make it a condition precedent, waivable only by the Buyer. It should require an unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) consent under DD-002 cl 11.2/11.3, with documentary evidence, delivered before Completion. Add a long-stop date and Buyer walk right. Ask the Seller for the current status since 22 September.

**9. Riverlark facility (cl 2/7)**
- **Seller:** A release "following Completion".
- **Playbook:** A current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Why it matters:** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, and the figure is "approximately" and stale. The letter (para 3) confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge exists. Under DD-003 cl 8.1, the facility contains a change-control provision.
- **Position:**
  - Require a payout letter dated close to Completion, including interest, break costs and fees.
  - Pay Riverlark directly from the funds flow and treat the amount as Debt in the price mechanics.
  - Require signed deeds of release and security discharges (including PPSR registrations) to be held in escrow and released at Completion.
  - Reject the post-completion release unless Amelia Frost approves it, and then only with an irrevocable bank undertaking.

**10. Funds flow and DD-005 bonuses**
- **Seller:** AUD 420k bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised.
- **Playbook:** AUD 420k plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Why it matters:** The *Company* is the employer, so it bears the liability, plus any payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs. The letter (para 5) admits the bonuses are not in the funds flow and that on-costs are unaddressed. "A matter for the Seller" protects us only if the bonuses are actually funded.
- **Position:**
  - Either treat the bonuses plus on-costs as Debt or Transaction Costs deducted from the price, or have the Seller fund them at Completion as a funds-flow line paid through payroll.
  - Add an indemnity for any shortfall.
  - Request a calculation of the on-costs.

**11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)**
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and "adequate".
- **Playbook:** Broaden the indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180k is not verified either way.
- **Why it matters:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on *cleared payment of every SOW3 fee*. The letter (para 4) confirms there is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment. The real risk is that the Company does not own IP embedded in the product. That risk is wider than one invoice.
- **Position:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover losses from any failure of the Company to own or be free to use Ironquay deliverables, and third-party claims arising from them.
  - Preserve the cure: payment of outstanding SOW3 fees plus a confirmatory assignment as a pre-Completion deliverable.
  - Request bank evidence on the AUD 180k. Do not assume it is paid or unpaid.

**12. DD-006 export incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6)**
- **Seller:** "Preliminary", and "not expected to be material".
- **Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate and require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand.
- **Why it matters:** "Not expected to be material" is an unsupported assertion. The Seller's own letter (para 6) says scope, access and any notification requirement are not established (around 1,240 records). We should not accept the Seller's assessment, and we should not overstate the incident either.
- **Position:**
  - Add pre-Completion covenants: preserve logs and evidence, complete the investigation, and give prompt written updates and access to findings.
  - Cooperate on any notification assessment.
  - Do not let Disclosure Letter para 6 qualify the relevant warranties.
  - Keep any specific indemnity open, with no fixed number.
  - Request an update on the position since 22 September.

**13. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k)**
- **Seller:** "Ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Playbook:** Assess them. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Why it matters:** The Seller's own letter (para 8) does not say whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. DD-008 and DD-011 must be read together. Its "ordinary course" label is therefore an assertion.
- **Position:** Request the contracts, the renewal and termination terms, the timing, and any accrual. Reserve the right to treat the renewals as Debt or covenant breaches depending on the findings. Do not concede "ordinary course" now.

**14. Tax and IP**
- **Seller:** "Settled under the general regime."
- **Playbook:** These terms remain open. Keep the categories separate. Do not assume unlimited liability or that anything is resolved.
- **Position:** Reject the characterisation. Tax and IP are open items in separate regimes, and their caps and periods are still to be negotiated.

**15. Title evidence**
- **Seller:** Relies on the DD-012 share register.
- **Playbook:** Require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is an internal source.
- **Why it matters:** The letter (para 10) itself says DD-012 is the source relied on, not verification.
- **Position:** Require:
  - an ASIC company extract;
  - share certificates and transfer history;
  - the constitution;
  - a PPSR search over the Seller and the shares;
  - Seller board resolutions authorising the sale.
  
  These sit alongside full title warranties in the fundamental regime.

### D. Minor items to verify (not accepted on the Seller's say-so)

- **Lease (DD-007):** Confirm it requires notification only. Add a covenant that the Seller gives the notice.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** Confirm the assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale. Check it for any change-of-control wording.

## 3. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the framing.** Strike the FINAL/[STANDARD]/efficiency-note premise. State in the cover note that all positions are open and that no principal-level agreement exists. Confirm this with Amelia Frost.
2. **Liability:** 25% / AUD 6.0m cap, limited to general claims. De minimis AUD 5k. Tipping basket of AUD 50k. 24-month general claims period. Reverse the "applies to all Claims" default.
3. **Fundamentals:** A separate title/capacity regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge provisions.
4. **Fraud:** A carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct, overriding all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. This is non-negotiable.
5. **Disclosure:** Delete general disclosure (DL 1.1–1.2). Specific fair disclosure only. No disclosure against title, fraud or the specific indemnities.
6. **Knowledge:** Delete cl 8.3. Seller knowledge qualifiers only by named persons after reasonable enquiry.
7. **Bluefen:** A Buyer-waivable condition precedent requiring an effective consent plus evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion.
8. **Riverlark:** A current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and releases/PPSR discharges at Completion. No post-completion release without Amelia Frost's approval and an irrevocable undertaking.
9. **Bonuses:** AUD 420k plus on-costs as an explicit funds-flow line or price deduction, with an indemnity.
10. **Ironquay:** A broadened IP indemnity, preserving the SOW3 payment-and-assignment cure. Verify the AUD 180k.
11. **DD-006:** Covenants to preserve, investigate and update. No acceptance of "not material", and no assumption of a breach.
12. **Sandbar, Tax and IP:** Reserve and assess. Keep the categories separate. Nothing is settled.
13. **Title:** Independent evidence pack in addition to DD-012.

**Authority note:** Neither the 20% cap nor the 18-month period may be offered or accepted without Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft. The same applies to any post-completion Riverlark release. None of these authorities exists today.
